# tboardfs mounted logs

This read-only tree exposes TensorBoard event data as files for training analysis.
This guide appears in each run directory that directly contains event files, including the mount root only when it directly contains event files.
A nested run appears as a directory below its parent.
Empty tabs and other empty directories are omitted.

## Directories

Metric tabs (`scalars`, `histograms`, `distributions`, `pr_curves`) contain training values and per-step tables; media tabs (`images`, `audio`, `videos`) contain stored media.
`text` contains text summaries; `meshes` geometry; `tensors` tensor values; `graphs` model graphs and run metadata; `hparams` run settings; `custom_scalars/layout.json` layouts; and `plugins` other plugin data.
`projector` and `profile` include run-directory sidecar files when available.
The mount exposes typed files by default; start it with `-r` or `--raw` to include original records.
Each `raw/<event-file>/<20-digit-byte-offset>.tfrecord` file contains one complete original TFRecord frame, named by byte offset in source order.

## Events and formats

The tree reads TensorFlow 1/2, Keras, PyTorch and PyTorch Lightning, tensorboardX, and compatible TensorBoard event writers.
It exposes scalar, histogram, distribution, PR-curve, image, audio, video, text, mesh, tensor, hyperparameter, custom-scalar, graph and plugin data.
A typed preview may be absent for an unsupported or malformed payload; enable the raw view to read the original frame.

Equivalent encodings are alternate views of the same logged values, not separate observations.
For example, scalar `<tag>.json`, `.tsv`, `.csv` and `.npz` files contain the same table; tensor `.npy` and `.json` files preview the same tensor.
Step-based files use zero-padded global steps.
Equal-step scalar rows are kept in producer order.

Media files keep the stored bytes and are not transcoded.
Extensions indicate likely formats, not guaranteed decodability.
`.bin` files contain opaque original tensor or field bytes, not a whole event frame; they are not, by themselves, evidence of a model checkpoint or weights.
